examples.solution_text:
The angles of $\triangle ADB$ add to $180^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}\angle ABD&=180^\circ-117^\circ-38^\circ\\&=25^\circ\end{aligned}$

$x=25^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel DC$).

Each angle of a rectangle is $90^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}\angle EDC&=90^\circ-31^\circ\\&=59^\circ\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\angle ECD&=90^\circ-31^\circ\\&=59^\circ\end{aligned}$

The angles of $\triangle DEC$ add to $180^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}x&=180^\circ-59^\circ-59^\circ\\&=62^\circ\end{aligned}$

The angles of $\triangle ABC$ add to $180^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}a&=180^\circ-114^\circ-27^\circ\\&=39^\circ\end{aligned}$

$b=27^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel DC$).

$\angle BCD=39^\circ+27^\circ=66^\circ$ (adding the two parts of the angle).

$c=66^\circ$ (angles at the ends of the same parallel side of an isosceles trapezium are equal).

a. $DC=AB=12\text{ cm}$ and $AD=BC=8\text{ cm}$ (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal).

$AM=15\div2=7.5\text{ cm}$ (the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other).

b. $QR=PQ=5.5\text{ cm}$ (all sides of a rhombus are equal).

$PQ=QR$, so $\triangle PQR$ is isosceles.

$\begin{aligned}\angle QPR=\angle PRQ&=(180^\circ-74^\circ)\div2\\&=53^\circ\end{aligned}$

Base angles are equal and the triangle's angles add to $180^\circ$.

$\angle SPQ=2\times53^\circ=106^\circ$ (diagonal $PR$ bisects the angle at $P$).

$\angle BCD=180^\circ-113^\circ=67^\circ$ (angles on the straight line $DCE$).

$\angle CDA=67^\circ$ (angles at the ends of the same parallel side of an isosceles trapezium are equal).

$\angle DAB=180^\circ-67^\circ=113^\circ$ (co-interior angles, $AB\parallel DC$).

$\angle ABC=113^\circ$ (angles at the ends of the same parallel side of an isosceles trapezium are equal).

a. Adjacent angles are co-interior on parallel sides and add to $180^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}(4x+6)+(2x+12)&=180\\6x+18&=180\\6x&=162\\x&=27\end{aligned}$

$\angle DAB=4(27)+6=114^\circ$.

$\angle BCD=114^\circ$ (opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal).

b. The interior angles of a quadrilateral add to $360^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}70+105+(4t+5)+(3t+5)&=360\\7t+185&=360\\7t&=175\\t&=25\end{aligned}$

$\angle QRS=4(25)+5=105^\circ$ and $\angle RSP=3(25)+5=80^\circ$.

$\angle SPQ+\angle PQR=70^\circ+105^\circ=175^\circ$, so $PS$ and $QR$ are not parallel (co-interior angles on transversal $PQ$ do not add to $180^\circ$).

Therefore $PQRS$ is not a parallelogram.

a. Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.

$\begin{aligned}\angle ACB&=\frac{180^\circ-4t^\circ}{2}\\&=(90-2t)^\circ\end{aligned}$

Angles on the straight line $BCD$ add to $180^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}\angle ACD&=180^\circ-(90-2t)^\circ\\&=(90+2t)^\circ\end{aligned}$

b. $\angle MKN=v^\circ$ (base angles of $\triangle KMN$, since $KM=MN$).

$\angle KMN=(180-2v)^\circ$ (angle sum of $\triangle KMN$).

$\angle KML=180^\circ-(180-2v)^\circ=2v^\circ$ (angles on the straight line $LMN$).

$\angle LKM=2v^\circ$ (base angles of $\triangle KLM$, since $KL=LM$).

$\begin{aligned}u+2v+2v&=180\\u+4v&=180\end{aligned}$

The angles of $\triangle KLM$ add to $180^\circ$.

Let the interior angles be $p^\circ$, $q^\circ$ and $h^\circ$.

$r+p=360$, $s+q=360$ and $t+h=360$ (angles at a point).

Adding gives $r+s+t+p+q+h=1080$.

$p+q+h=180$ (angle sum of a triangle).

$\begin{aligned}r+s+t&=1080-180\\&=900\end{aligned}$

Every triangle has interior angle sum $180^\circ$, so the result is always $900$.

The angles between the unequal sides of a kite are equal.

$\begin{aligned}3z+6&=5z-50\\2z&=56\\z&=28\end{aligned}$

$\angle KLM=\angle KNM=3(28)+6=90^\circ$.

The interior angles of a quadrilateral add to $360^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}y&=360^\circ-120^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ\\&=60^\circ\end{aligned}$

The interior angles of a quadrilateral add to $360^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}(3z+4)+(5z+16)+(2z+24)+(4z+36)&=360\\14z+80&=360\\14z&=280\\z&=20\end{aligned}$

$\angle DAB=64^\circ$, $\angle ABC=116^\circ$, $\angle BCD=64^\circ$ and $\angle CDA=116^\circ$ (substituting $z=20$).

$\angle DAB+\angle ABC=64^\circ+116^\circ=180^\circ$, so $AD\parallel BC$ (converse of the co-interior angle relationship, transversal $AB$).

$\angle DAB+\angle CDA=64^\circ+116^\circ=180^\circ$, so $AB\parallel DC$ (converse of the co-interior angle relationship, transversal $AD$).

Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

examples.derivation: Triangle ADB gives angle ABD = 180 − 117 − 38 = 25°. Alternate angles with AB parallel to DC give x = 25°.
The rectangle gives angles EDC and ECD of 90 − 31 = 59°. Triangle DEC gives x = 180 − 59 − 59 = 62°.
Triangle ABC gives a = 180 − 114 − 27 = 39°. Alternate angles give b = 27°. Thus angle BCD = 66°, and the equal base angles of the isosceles trapezium give c = 66°.

Given equal sides yield AD=p cm and CD=q cm. Kite diagonals give angle BMC=90°. Equal kite angles give angle ADC=105°. The quadrilateral sum gives angle BCD=360°−90°−105°−105°=60°; axis AC bisects it, so angle BCM=30°. The coordinates preserve equal side pairs and the stated angles. The relocated whole-angle labels remain associated with A, B and D and are separated from M and its right-angle marker.

Parallelogram properties give DC = 12 cm, AD = 8 cm and AM = 15/2 = 7.5 cm. Rhombus properties give QR = 5.5 cm. Equal sides in triangle PQR give both base angles as (180 − 74)/2 = 53°. Diagonal bisection gives angle SPQ = 106°.
At R, angle PRQ = 180 − 76 − 48 = 56°. Since PR = RQ, angle RQP = (180 − 56)/2 = 62°. Triangle RQC gives angle RQC = 180 − 90 − 48 = 42°. The straight line BQC gives x = 180 − 62 − 42 = 76°.

Equilateral ABC gives angle PAQ=60°. Triangle APQ gives angle AQP=180°−60°−97°=23°. Straight line AQC gives x=180°−23°=157°. The coordinates and angle arms agree with these relationships. The revised 4 mm radius and 1.5 eccentricity place the 23° label beside Q's arc, separated from the 97° annotation at P.
The exterior angle gives angle BCD = 180 − 113 = 67°. Equal base angles give angle CDA = 67°. Co-interior angles give angle DAB = 113°, and equal upper base angles give angle ABC = 113°.

Part a: 6x + 18 = 180 gives x = 27, angle DAB = 114° and opposite angle BCD = 114°. Part b: 7t + 185 = 360 gives t = 25, angle QRS = 105° and angle RSP = 80°. The adjacent angles at P and Q total 175°, disproving PS parallel to QR and therefore disproving a parallelogram.

Part a: each base angle is (180 − 4t)/2 = 90 − 2t degrees; its adjacent exterior angle is 90 + 2t degrees. Part b: KM = MN gives angle MKN = v and angle KMN = 180 − 2v degrees. The straight line gives angle KML = 2v degrees. KL = LM gives angle LKM = 2v degrees. Triangle KLM therefore gives u + 4v = 180.
Each reflex angle and its interior angle total 360°. Adding the three pairs gives 1080°. Subtracting the invariant triangle interior sum of 180° gives r + s + t = 900.

The constructed parallel line transfers p and q to adjacent angles inside angle ACB by alternate-angle equality. Since ABC is equilateral, angle ACB = 60°, hence p + q = 60. The construction appears only in the solution.
Equal kite angles give 3z + 6 = 5z − 50, so z = 28. Both angles are 90°. The quadrilateral sum gives y = 360 − 120 − 90 − 90 = 60°.
Angle TXY = 90 − 60 = 30°. XT = XY gives angle XTY = (180 − 30)/2 = 75°. Similarly angle ZTW = 75°. Around T, the smaller angle YTZ = 360 − 75 − 60 − 75 = 150°, so the reflex angle is 210°.

The quadrilateral sum gives 14z + 80 = 360, hence z = 20. The successive interior angles are 64°, 116°, 64° and 116°. Supplementary co-interior angles on transversal AB establish AD parallel to BC; the separate test on transversal AD establishes AB parallel to DC. Both pairs establish a parallelogram.

The quadrilateral sum gives 4x + 200 = 360, hence x = 40. Angles C and D are 120° and 60°. The two right angles on transversal AB establish AD parallel to BC. The supplementary angles on DC test that same pair. Angles A and D total 150°, disproving AB parallel to DC. Exactly one parallel pair establishes a trapezium.
